docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/flash.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The "flash" messages: a message to display ONCE, on the NEXT
# page (see example 20). It is the natural complement of the
# "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern used by all the forms of the application:
# a successful POST does not build a page, it redirects (302) to a
# GET page; the message, however, must survive the redirect.
#
# Flask stores them in the SESSION, that is, in a cookie SIGNED by the
# secret key (SECRET_KEY): the server remains STATELESS, it keeps nothing in
# memory between two requests. The browser can read this cookie (it is
# not encrypted), but not modify it without the signature giving it away.
#
# A message does not contain a text, but a translation KEY and its
# parameters: it is translated at display time, in the language of
# the page (see templates/layout.html). Its category: "success" (displayed at
# the top of the page) or "danger" (an error, displayed at the bottom).
# =========================================================================
from flask import flash


def flash_success(key: str, **params):
    flash({"key": key, "params": params}, "success")


def flash_error(key: str, **params):
    flash({"key": key, "params": params}, "danger")

The flash messages from Example 20. A message is not text, but a dictionary: the translation key and its parameters. It will be translated at the time of display, by the template, into the page’s language. [Flask] stores the messages in the session, which is a cookie: to do this, it converts them to JSON, which accepts a dictionary of strings. The message category ([success] or [danger], the color names from [Bootstrap]) determines its location: at the top of the page for a success, at the bottom for an error.

docs.title: 11.14.5. web/errors.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/errors.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How the errors become HTML pages. Three handlers share
# the work (see example 24):
#
#   1. an InvalidSession (account deleted since the login) -> back to
#      the login page, as for an expired session;
#   2. an HTTP error: abort(400), abort(403) (insufficient role), unknown
#      page (404), unsupported method (405), anti-CSRF token
#      missing or wrong (400)... -> the error page, with the original code;
#   3. any other exception (a real anomaly) -> written in the log
#      of the server, with its stack trace; the user sees the
#      500 error page - never the stack trace.
# =========================================================================
from flask import current_app, redirect, render_template, url_for
from werkzeug.exceptions import HTTPException

from rdvmedecins.auth.auth_service import AuthService
from rdvmedecins.auth.security import InvalidSession
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import ErrorModel
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_error

MESSAGES = {
    400: "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST",
    403: "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN",
    404: "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND",
}


def error_page(code: int):
    model = ErrorModel("ERROR_PAGE.TITLE", None, code, MESSAGES.get(code, "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR"))
    # the page keeps the error code (404 stays 404...)
    return render_template("error.html", model=model), code


def register(app):

    @app.errorhandler(InvalidSession)
    def invalid_session(e):
        response = redirect(url_for("auth.show_login"))
        AuthService.clear_token(response)
        flash_error("ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED")
        return response

    @app.errorhandler(HTTPException)
    def http_error(e: HTTPException):
        return error_page(e.code or 500)

    # Exception: the parent class of all the exceptions; this handler
    # only receives those that no more specific handler has processed
    @app.errorhandler(Exception)
    def anomaly(e: Exception):
        current_app.logger.exception("unexpected error")
        return error_page(500)

The error handlers in Example 24:

  • lines 31–34: the error page, with the original error code (a 404 page remains a 404 response) and a translated message chosen based on the code;
  • lines 39–44: an account deleted since login: redirect to the login page, as with an expired session;
  • lines 46–48: all HTTP errors: [abort(403)], an unknown page (404), a forbidden method (405), a missing or invalid anti-CSRF token (400, handled by [CSRFProtect])...;
  • lines 52–55: any other exception, i.e., a true anomaly (a programming error, a database that has become inaccessible). [current_app.logger] is the application log (an object of the standard module [logging]); its method [exception] writes the message to it, followed by the call stack of the current exception. The user, however, sees only the 500 error page: never the call stack, which would reveal internal details of the application. [Flask] always selects the most specific handler: a HTTP error is handled by the second handler, not by this one.

docs.title: 11.14.6. web/application_model.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/application_model.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cache / facade of the business layer (the equivalent of the
# [ApplicationModel] class of the previous versions of the application): the
# lists of doctors and of clients are read once at startup, then
# served from memory.
#
# These lists can CHANGE (the ADMIN adds, edits, deletes
# doctors and clients): each write therefore goes through this facade,
# which reloads the list concerned right after. This is the whole point of a
# SINGLE entry point to the business layer: the rule "write =>
# cache reload" is written only here.
#
# A single object for the whole application, used by requests
# processed IN PARALLEL, on several threads. A list is therefore never modified
# in place: it is REPLACED entirely by a new one. In Python,
# the assignment of an attribute is atomic: a thread that reads the list sees
# the old or the new one, never a half-built list.
# =========================================================================
from datetime import date

from rdvmedecins.domain.schedule import DoctorDaySchedule
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Slot, Doctor, Appointment
from rdvmedecins.business.person_data import PersonData
from rdvmedecins.business.business import Business


# same contract as the business layer (Business)
class ApplicationModel:

    def __init__(self, business: Business):
        self._business = business
        # initial loading of the two lists, at application startup.
        # A read error (unreachable database...) is not caught:
        # it stops the server, rather than letting it start "empty"
        self._doctors: list[Doctor] = []
        self._clients: list[Client] = []
        self._reload_doctors()
        self._reload_clients()

    def _reload_doctors(self):
        self._doctors = list(self._business.get_all_doctors())

    def _reload_clients(self):
        self._clients = list(self._business.get_all_clients())

    # ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

    def get_all_doctors(self) -> list[Doctor]:
        return self._doctors

    def get_all_clients(self) -> list[Client]:
        return self._clients

    # the doctor whose user account is [user_id] - used to preselect,
    # for a connected doctor, their own schedule
    def get_doctor_by_user_id(self, user_id: int) -> Doctor | None:
        return next((d for d in self._doctors if d.user_id == user_id), None)

    # ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    def get_all_slots(self, doctor_id: int) -> list[Slot]:
        return self._business.get_all_slots(doctor_id)

    def get_doctor_day_appointments(self, doctor_id: int, day: date) -> list[Appointment]:
        return self._business.get_doctor_day_appointments(doctor_id, day)

    def get_client_by_id(self, id: int) -> Client | None:
        return self._business.get_client_by_id(id)

    def get_doctor_by_id(self, id: int) -> Doctor | None:
        return self._business.get_doctor_by_id(id)

    def get_appointment_by_id(self, id: int) -> Appointment | None:
        return self._business.get_appointment_by_id(id)

    def get_slot_by_id(self, id: int) -> Slot | None:
        return self._business.get_slot_by_id(id)

    def get_doctor_day_schedule(self, doctor_id: int, day: date) -> DoctorDaySchedule | None:
        return self._business.get_doctor_day_schedule(doctor_id, day)

    # no cache here: it is the most recent data that matters (a patient
    # who has just edited or deleted their account)
    def get_client_by_user_id(self, user_id: int) -> Client | None:
        return self._business.get_client_by_user_id(user_id)

    def get_client_upcoming_appointments(self, client_id: int) -> list[Appointment]:
        return self._business.get_client_upcoming_appointments(client_id)

    def add_appointment(self, day: date, slot: Slot, client: Client) -> Appointment:
        return self._business.add_appointment(day, slot, client)

    def delete_appointment(self, appointment: Appointment) -> None:
        self._business.delete_appointment(appointment)

    # ------------------------------------------------ writes => reload

    def add_doctor(self, data: PersonData) -> Doctor:
        doctor = self._business.add_doctor(data)
        self._reload_doctors()
        return doctor

    def edit_doctor(self, id: int, data: PersonData) -> Doctor:
        doctor = self._business.edit_doctor(id, data)
        self._reload_doctors()
        return doctor

    def delete_doctor(self, id: int) -> None:
        self._business.delete_doctor(id)
        self._reload_doctors()

    def add_client(self, data: PersonData) -> Client:
        client = self._business.add_client(data)
        self._reload_clients()
        return client

    def edit_client(self, id: int, data: PersonData) -> Client:
        client = self._business.edit_client(id, data)
        self._reload_clients()
        return client

    def delete_client(self, id: int) -> None:
        self._business.delete_client(id)
        self._reload_clients()

The web layer cache and its interface to the business layer:

  • lines 32–40: the lists of doctors and patients are read once, at startup. They are used every time the calendar is displayed (the drop-down list of doctors, the list of patients): keeping them in memory avoids two SQL requests per page. A read error is not caught: it causes the application to crash at startup (see “Common Problems”);
  • lines 50–59: data retrieved from the cache. [get_doctor_by_user_id] identifies the logged-in doctor to preselect their own calendar;
  • lines 63–96: the other read operations, and the appointments, are simply relayed to the business layer. [get_client_by_user_id] does not use the cache: a patient who has just modified or deleted their account must see the most recent data;
  • lines 100–126: Each update to doctors or clients refreshes the relevant list. This is the benefit of a single entry point to the business layer: the rule “update, then refresh the cache” is implemented only here.

This unique object is used by requests processed in parallel across multiple threads: therefore, a list is never modified in place (by [append] or [remove]); instead, it is replaced entirely with a new one. In [Python], assigning an attribute is atomic: a thread reading the list sees either the old or the new version, never a partially constructed list. Therefore, no lock is needed.

[ApplicationModel] adheres to the [Business] contract (it has the same methods as [BusinessService]): for the controllers, it is the business layer. We could remove the cache without touching the controllers by directly placing [BusinessService] inside [app.extensions].

docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/validation.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What is needed to DISPLAY AGAIN a refused form: the input errors
# field by field, and the fields to outline in red.
# =========================================================================
from flask_wtf import FlaskForm

from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import FormState, Message


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the validated form (see forms/forms.py) -> the dictionary
# field -> key of the message, keeping only the first message of each
# field: { "last_name": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", ... }
#
# Our messages are translation keys ("ERRORS...."). A message that
# WTForms has written itself (in English) is replaced by the key
# ERRORS.INVALID_FORM.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def errors_of(form: FlaskForm) -> dict[str, str]:
    errors = {}
    for field, messages in form.errors.items():
        message = str(messages[0])
        errors[field] = message if message.startswith("ERRORS.") else "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM"
    return errors


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the form fields concerned by each "input" business error
# (a duplicate): they are outlined in red, the message being at the bottom of the page
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS = {
    "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN": ["login"],
    "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS": ["first_name", "last_name"],
    "ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS": ["first_name", "last_name"],
}


# the state of a form to display (again): a message under each field
# refused by the validation (errors), and the fields to outline in red,
# those plus possible others (other_fields)
def state(errors: dict[str, str], other_fields: list[str] | None = None) -> FormState:
    return FormState(dict(errors), set(errors) | set(other_fields or []))


# THE error message of the page, displayed at the bottom of the page: [error] if
# there is one, otherwise "The form contains errors." if there are
# field errors, otherwise nothing
def page_message(errors: dict[str, str], error: Message | None) -> Message | None:
    if error is not None:
        return error
    return Message("ERRORS.INVALID_FORM") if errors else None

What is needed to redisplay a rejected form:

  • lines 21–26: the errors from a [WTForms] form (example 19), in the form of a “field → message key” dictionary, keeping only the first message for each field. The messages from our validators are translation keys ([ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED], see [forms/forms.py]); a message that [WTForms] would have generated itself, in English, is replaced by a generic key;
  • lines 33–36: Some business-logic errors pertain to specific fields—such as a username that’s already taken or a name with the same spelling. Their error messages appear at the bottom of the page, but the affected fields are highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct (see the screenshot of the name with the same spelling above);
  • lines 43–44: the state of a form to be redisplayed: the messages below the fields, and all fields to be highlighted in red. [set(errors)] is the set of keys in the dictionary; the operator [|] performs a union of two sets;
  • lines 50–53: the general footer message.

docs.title: 11.14.8. web/utils.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/utils.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small utility functions of the web layer:
#   - labels: "Mme Alice DURAND";
#   - dates: "yyyy-mm-dd", times "8:05", days "Wednesday 23 September 2026";
#   - input: reading a positive integer sent by the browser;
#   - user: the connected user, and their patient (Client entity).
# =========================================================================
import re
from datetime import date, datetime

from babel.dates import format_date
from flask import g

from rdvmedecins.auth.security import InvalidSession
from rdvmedecins.auth.connected_user import ConnectedUser
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Slot, Person

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- labels


# "Mme Alice DURAND"
def label(p: Person) -> str:
    return f"{p.title} {p.first_name} {p.last_name}"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- dates

# the format of the dates in the URLs and in the <input type="date"> field
ISO_FORMAT = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")


# the date, if [text] is a date that exists in the yyyy-mm-dd format; None otherwise.
# strptime checks that the date exists: "2026-02-30" is refused
def valid_date(text: str | None) -> date | None:
    if text is None or not ISO_FORMAT.fullmatch(text):
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except ValueError:
        return None


def iso(day: date) -> str:
    return day.isoformat()


# "8:05" rather than "8:5"
def format_time(h: int, m: int) -> str:
    return f"{h}:{m:02d}"


def time(s: Slot) -> str:
    return f"{format_time(s.start_hour, s.start_minute)} - {format_time(s.end_hour, s.end_minute)}"


# "mercredi 23 septembre 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026", according to the
# language of the request (g.language). The Babel format: EEEE the day of the
# week in full, d the day, MMMM the month in full, y the year
def format_day(day: date) -> str:
    return format_date(day, "EEEE d MMMM y", locale=g.language)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- input


# "3" -> 3 ; "", "abc", "-2", "+2", None -> None
def positive_integer(value: str | None) -> int | None:
    if value is None or not re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,9}", value):
        return None
    n = int(value)
    return n if n > 0 else None


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- user


# the connected user (see auth/security.py). The protected actions are
# only called if they exist; as a precaution, their absence is handled
# as an expired session.
def user() -> ConnectedUser:
    if g.user is None:
        raise InvalidSession()
    return g.user


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The patient (Client entity) that corresponds to the connected user.
#
# The JWT token only contains the id of the ACCOUNT (users.id). For a USER
# role, the corresponding client is found thanks to the clients.user column.
#
# If there is none, the account has been deleted since the
# login while its token is still valid: it is handled as an expired
# session (see InvalidSession).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def connected_patient(application) -> Client:
    patient = application.get_client_by_user_id(user().user_id)
    if patient is None:
        raise InvalidSession()
    return patient

Utility functions used by multiple controllers:

  • line 24: a person’s title, “Mme Alice DURAND”;
  • lines 31–42: parsing a date in the [yyyy-mm-dd] format, which is the same as that used for the URL entries in the calendar ([day=2026-09-26]) and the [<input type="date">] field. The regular expression checks the format ([fullmatch]: the entire string must match), while [strptime] checks for the existence of the date. An invalid date results in [None]: the action determines the outcome;
  • lines 50–51: the format [02d] outputs a two-digit integer, padded with zeros: [8:05];
  • lines 61–62: a date written out in full, in the language of the query, with [Babel] (example 16). The format is explicitly specified here: [EEEE], the day of the week spelled out; [d], the day; [MMMM], the month spelled out; [y], the year;
  • lines 69–73: reading an identifier sent by the browser (a parameter of URL, a hidden field). [\d{1,9}]: one to nine digits, which excludes characters, spaces, and numbers too large for a [INT] column. Anything coming from the browser may have been modified: it must be verified before use;
  • lines 82–85: the logged-in user; its absence (which should not occur in a protected action) is treated as an expired session;
  • lines 98–102: the patient (the entity [Client]) corresponding to the logged-in user. The token contains only the account ID: the patient is identified by the [clients.user] column. If it does not exist, it means the account has been deleted since the user logged in.

docs.title: 11.15. The forms and templates for the views
11.15.1. forms/rules.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# forms/rules.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The input rules common to the "person" forms, and the FILTERS
# of WTForms (see example 19): functions that transform the value
# received BEFORE the validation.
# =========================================================================
TITLES = ("Mr", "Mme", "Melle")

# login: lower-case letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore - 30 characters at most
LOGIN_FORMAT = r"^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$"

# minimum length of a password CHOSEN by a patient
PASSWORD_MIN = 6


# "  dupont " -> "dupont" ; "   " -> None
def clean(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    return value.strip() or None


# "  Dupont " -> "dupont": a login is always in lower case
def login(value):
    value = clean(value)
    return value.lower() if isinstance(value, str) else value


# an empty field -> None; for a password, the spaces are NOT removed
# (they can be part of it)
def empty_to_none(value):
    return value if value else None


# the hidden field [version]: an integer, or None if it is missing or empty.
# A text that is not a number: a ValueError, that WTForms turns
# into a field error, with this message (a translation key)
def version(value):
    if value in (None, ""):
        return None
    try:
        return int(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError("ERRORS.INVALID_FORM")

Input rules common to all forms, and the [WTForms] filters (example 19):

  • lines 8–14: allowed titles, the format of a username (lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore, up to 30 characters), and the minimum length of a password chosen by a patient;
  • Lines 18–21: The spaces surrounding an entry are removed; an empty entry becomes [None]. [a or b] is equivalent to [b] if [a] is “false” (in this case, an empty string);
  • lines 25–27: a username is always in lowercase;
  • lines 32–33: for a password, spaces are not removed, as they may be part of the password;
  • lines 39–45: the hidden version field (the optimistic lock): an integer, or [None]. A filter that returns a value like [ValueError] triggers a field error, with the error message matching that of the exception: a browser that submits anything other than a number would receive the “invalid form” error.

docs.title: 11.15.2. forms/forms.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# forms/forms.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fields of the "person" forms and their constraints (see examples
# 19 and 28). Three forms share the same identity fields
# (title, first name, last name):
#
#   PersonFields                  title, first name, last name
#    ├─ PersonForm                + OPTIONAL login / password, version
#    │                              (the ADMIN adds or edits a doctor / client)
#    ├─ RegistrationForm          + MANDATORY login / password / confirmation
#    │                              (a patient creates their account)
#    └─ MyAccountForm             + login, optional new password,
#                                   mandatory CURRENT password, version
#                                   (a patient edits their account)
#
# A WTForms class that inherits from another one also inherits its fields.
#
# BINDING: PersonForm() itself reads the fields with the same name of the
# current POST request (request.form), and applies its filters to them
# (superfluous spaces removed, login in lower case...).
# VALIDATION: form.validate() then checks the constraints of each
# field, in order; the first one that fails stores its message in
# form.<field>.errors. These messages are translation KEYS (see i18n/*.json).
#
# The forms are only used here to read and validate the input: the views
# write their <input> tags themselves, from the view models
# (see models/view_models.py).
# =========================================================================
from flask_wtf import FlaskForm
from wtforms import PasswordField, StringField
from wtforms.validators import AnyOf, DataRequired, InputRequired, Length, Optional, Regexp

from rdvmedecins.forms import rules


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
class PersonFields(FlaskForm):

    title = StringField(validators=[AnyOf(rules.TITLES, message="ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")])

    # maximum lengths = those of the SQL columns (VARCHAR(20)).
    # DataRequired stops the validation of the field if it is empty: the message
    # of Length is therefore never added to that one
    first_name = StringField(filters=[rules.clean], validators=[
        DataRequired("ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED"),
        Length(max=20, message="ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG")])

    last_name = StringField(filters=[rules.clean], validators=[
        DataRequired("ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED"),
        Length(max=20, message="ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG")])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
class PersonForm(PersonFields):

    # optional (see business/person_data.py): Optional stops the validation of an
    # empty field, without error
    login = StringField(filters=[rules.login], validators=[
        Optional(), Regexp(rules.LOGIN_FORMAT, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

    # optional; 72 characters at most (beyond that, bcrypt ignores the rest)
    password = PasswordField(filters=[rules.empty_to_none], validators=[
        Optional(strip_whitespace=False), Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    # hidden field of the edit form (optimistic lock)
    version = StringField(filters=[rules.version])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ registration of a patient
class RegistrationForm(PersonFields):

    # InputRequired: the input must not be empty
    login = StringField(filters=[rules.login], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED"),
        Regexp(rules.LOGIN_FORMAT, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

    # two Length constraints, each with its message
    password = PasswordField(filters=[rules.empty_to_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED"),
        Length(min=rules.PASSWORD_MIN, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT"),
        Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    confirmation = PasswordField(filters=[rules.empty_to_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED")])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage my account"
class MyAccountForm(PersonFields):

    login = StringField(filters=[rules.login], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED"),
        Regexp(rules.LOGIN_FORMAT, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

    # optional: empty = password unchanged
    password = PasswordField(filters=[rules.empty_to_none], validators=[
        Optional(strip_whitespace=False),
        Length(min=rules.PASSWORD_MIN, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT"),
        Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    confirmation = PasswordField(filters=[rules.empty_to_none])

    # the CURRENT password, required for any edit of the account
    current_password = PasswordField(filters=[rules.empty_to_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED")])

    version = StringField(filters=[rules.version])
  • Lines 38–51: the fields common to all three forms: title, first name, last name. The validator messages are translation keys: the view will translate them into the page’s language. The [AnyOf] validator accepts a value from a list. The maximum lengths are those of the SQL columns: a longer entry would be rejected by the database;
  • lines 55–67: the administrator form: a login and an optional password (the [Optional] validator stops validating an empty field without reporting an error; [strip_whitespace=False]: a password consisting of spaces is not considered empty), and the version;
  • lines 71–85: the patient registration form: username, password, and confirmation are required. Two validators, [Length], each with its own message: too short, too long;
  • lines 89–107: “Manage my account”: an optional new password, and the current password, which is required for any changes.

A [WTForms] class that inherits from another class, inherits its fields: the three forms share the fields of [PersonFields]. The comparison of the password and its confirmation is not handled by the [EqualTo] validator (Example 19), but is performed by the action, which thus selects the message and the relevant field.

Note that these forms are used only to read and validate user input: the views do not call the [WTForms] fields to render them (Example 18); instead, they write their own [<input>] tags based on the view templates. This approach keeps the views identical across all three forms and gives the action complete control over what is displayed (never a password, for example). This is also the approach used in previous versions of the application.

# =========================================================================
# models/view_models.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The "view models": what each action passes to its
# view, under the name [model]. They are dataclasses: objects built
# in one go by the action, that the view merely reads
# ({{ model.schedule.rows }}...).
#
# Rule followed by all the pages: no logic in the views. The
# actions prepare data ALREADY formatted ("Mme Marie
# PELISSIER", "8:00 - 8:20", selected = True...) and already filtered according to
# the role of the user; the views merely place them in the HTML.
#
# Each page model has two fields, read by the layout (templates/layout.html):
# page_title, the key of the page title, and error, THE error message of
# the page, displayed at the bottom of the page (None: no error).
# =========================================================================
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from rdvmedecins.auth.captcha import Captcha
from rdvmedecins.forms import rules


# a message to translate: its key, and its parameters
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Message:
    key: str
    params: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


# an option of a drop-down list (doctor, patient)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionView:
    id: int
    label: str
    selected: bool


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ login
@dataclass
class LoginModel:
    page_title: str
    error: Message | None
    login: str
    captcha: Captcha


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ schedule
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScheduleRowView:
    slot_id: int
    time: str  # "8:00 - 8:20"
    free: bool
    patient: str | None  # name displayed for a booked slot; None = "Booked"
    mine: bool  # the appointment of the connected patient
    bookable: bool  # display the "Book" button?
    book_url: str
    appointment_id: int | None  # filled only if the "Cancel" button is displayed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScheduleView:
    doctor: str
    day: str
    rows: list[ScheduleRowView]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BookingView:
    slot_id: int
    time: str
    clients: list[OptionView]  # ADMIN / DOCTOR: the patients to choose from
    patient: str | None  # USER: the patient is themselves


@dataclass
class ScheduleModel:
    page_title: str
    error: Message | None
    doctors: list[OptionView]
    doctor_id: int | None
    day: str  # "yyyy-mm-dd"
    schedule: ScheduleView | None
    booking: BookingView | None
    back_url: str  # the displayed schedule, without booking dialog
    # patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the message that explains
    # why there is no "Book" button
    info: str | None


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ "person" forms

# the values displayed in the fields of the form (never the password)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonValues:
    title: str = "Mr"
    first_name: str = ""
    last_name: str = ""
    login: str = ""
    version: int | None = None


# the state of a refused form: the message displayed UNDER each field
# (field -> key of the message), and the fields to outline in red (Bootstrap
# class is-invalid): those that have a message, plus possible others
# (duplicate first + last names, login taken...)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FormState:
    errors: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    invalid_fields: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    def error_of(self, field: str) -> str | None:
        return self.errors.get(field)

    def invalid_class(self, field: str) -> str:
        return "is-invalid" if field in self.invalid_fields else ""


# an option of the list of titles
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TitleOption:
    value: str
    selected: bool


# what the common fragment person_fields.html uses (title, first name, last name):
# a base class, from which the three form models inherit
@dataclass
class FormView:
    page_title: str
    error: Message | None
    values: PersonValues
    state: FormState

    # a property: is read like an attribute (model.titles), but is computed
    @property
    def titles(self) -> list[TitleOption]:
        return [TitleOption(t, t == self.values.title) for t in rules.TITLES]

    @property
    def password_min(self) -> int:
        return rules.PASSWORD_MIN


@dataclass
class PersonFormModel(FormView):
    creating: bool  # True: add; False: edit
    action: str  # URL of the POST
    list_url: str


@dataclass
class RegistrationModel(FormView):
    pass


@dataclass
class MyAccountModel(FormView):
    pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ doctor / client lists

# the translation keys specific to each type of person
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonKeys:
    title: str  # "Doctors"
    add: str  # "Add a doctor"
    edit: str  # "Edit a doctor"
    empty: str  # "No doctors."
    confirm_delete: str  # "Delete this doctor and their account?"
    added: str  # "Doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
    edited: str
    deleted: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonView:
    title: str
    first_name: str
    last_name: str
    login: str
    edit_url: str
    delete_url: str


@dataclass
class PersonListModel:
    page_title: str
    error: Message | None
    keys: PersonKeys
    add_url: str
    persons: list[PersonView]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient's area
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AppointmentView:
    id: int
    day: str
    time: str
    doctor: str
    schedule_url: str


@dataclass
class AreaModel:
    page_title: str
    error: Message | None
    patient: str
    appointments: list[AppointmentView]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ error page
@dataclass
class ErrorModel:
    page_title: str
    error: Message | None
    code: int
    message: str

View models (*view models*): what each action passes to its view, under the name [model]. The rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. Actions prepare data that is already formatted (“Mme Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; views simply place this data into the HTML.

  • lines 26–28: a message to be translated: a key and its parameters. [field(default_factory=dict)]: the default value is a new, empty dictionary for each object. You cannot write [= {}]: this dictionary would be created only once and shared by all objects;
  • lines 33–36: an option from a drop-down list;
  • lines 41–45: the login page template. Each page template has two fields read by the template: [page_title], the page title key, and [error], the error message displayed at the bottom of the page;
  • lines 50–58: a row in the calendar, already populated for the logged-in user: [patient] is equivalent to [None] for a time slot occupied by another patient, when the user is a patient (the view will display “Booked”) ; [bookable] indicates whether to display the “Book” button; [appointment_id] is populated only if the “Cancel” button is to be displayed. All these decisions are made by the action;
  • lines 69–73: the booking window: the list of patients for an administrator or doctor, the patient’s name for a patient;
  • lines 77–88: the calendar page template;
  • lines 108–116: the state of a rejected form, with two methods called by the views: the message for a field, and the CSS class that highlights it in red;
  • lines 129–142: the base class for the three form templates, used by the common fragment [person_fields.html]. Its two properties calculate the list of titles (including the selected title) and the minimum length of a password;
  • Lines 146–158: The three form templates inherit from [FormView]. A [dataclass] that inherits from another adds its fields to those of its parent class;
  • lines 166–174: translation keys specific to doctors or clients: the same view displays both lists;
  • lines 198–211: the patient area;
  • lines 216–220: the error page.

docs.title: 11.16. The Web Layer: Controllers
docs.text:
The [controllers] folder contains one blueprint per part of the application (the login controller, [controllers/auth.py], was introduced with authentication):

BlueprintAddresses[language][GET /language/<code>][schedule][GET /schedule], [POST /schedule/book], [POST /schedule/cancel][doctors], [clients][/doctors/...], [/clients/...]: list, add, edit, delete[registration][POST /register/access], [GET], and [POST /register][area][/my-area], [/my-area/cancel], [/my-account], [/my-account/delete]

All actions follow the same pattern: read and validate the request, call the business layer (via [ApplicationModel]), build the view model; or, for an action such as POST, post a flash message and redirect (flow PRG, example 20).

docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# controllers/language.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two FR / EN buttons of the
# navigation bar. Public route: one must be able to change the language before
# logging in.
#
# The choice is remembered in a cookie: on each following request, the
# set_language function (see rdvmedecins/__init__.py) reads it again and sets the
# language of the request (g.language). Then we go back to the page we came from.
# =========================================================================
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from flask import Blueprint, abort, current_app, redirect, request

from rdvmedecins.auth.security import public
from rdvmedecins.web.translator import LANGUAGE_COOKIE, LANGUAGES

language = Blueprint("language", __name__)


@language.get("/language/<code>")
@public
def change(code: str):
    if code not in LANGUAGES:
        abort(404)  # -> 404 error page (see web/errors.py)
    response = redirect(origin_page())
    response.set_cookie(LANGUAGE_COOKIE, code, max_age=timedelta(days=365), path="/",
                        httponly=True, samesite="Lax", secure=current_app.config["COOKIE_SECURE"])
    return response


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the previous page, according to the HTTP "Referer" header sent by the
# browser. Only its path (/schedule?...) is kept: redirecting to
# a full address provided by the request would make it possible to send
# the user to another site (so-called "open redirect" flaw).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def origin_page() -> str:
    referer = request.headers.get("Referer")
    if not referer:
        return "/"
    url = urlsplit(referer)
    path = url.path
    # "//site.com/..." would be understood by the browser as an address
    # on ANOTHER site: refused too
    if not url.scheme or not path.startswith("/") or path.startswith("//") \
            or path.startswith("/language/"):
        return "/"
    return f"{path}?{url.query}" if url.query else path

The language selection from Example 22, with two additional precautions in [origin_page] (lines 40–51): a [Referer] without a schema ([http], [https]) is not a complete address, and a [Referer]—which would itself be a [/language/...] address—would redirect to this action, creating a loop. In both cases, the user is redirected back to the site’s root. The cookie’s lifetime is specified by a [timedelta]: [set_cookie] accepts this just as well as a number of seconds.

docs.title: 11.16.2. controllers/schedule.py
docs.text:
The application’s main page, for all roles.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/schedule.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The schedule page: choice of a doctor and a day, schedule of this
# doctor on that day, booking and cancelling of appointments.
#
#   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23              the page
#   GET  /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7        the same page, with
#                                                          the booking dialog
#                                                          of slot 7 open
#   POST /schedule/book                                    creates an appointment
#   POST /schedule/cancel                                  cancels an appointment
#
# The whole page is described by its URL: it can be reloaded, bookmarked,
# the "Back" button of the browser can be used - without a single line
# of JavaScript.
#
# What each one sees and can do:
#
#   | role          | booked slot displayed             | Book               | Cancel  |
#   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
#   | ADMIN, DOCTOR | name of the patient               | for a patient      | yes     |
#   |               |                                   | chosen in a list   |         |
#   | USER (patient)| "Booked", or THEIR name if it is  | for themselves, if | no (*)  |
#   |               | their own appointment             | they have no       |         |
#   |               |                                   | upcoming appt      |         |
#
#   (*) the patient cancels their appointment from their "My area" page.
#
# CONFIDENTIALITY: for a patient, the name of the OTHER patients is not
# simply hidden by the view - it is never put in the model
# passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
# not even hidden (a simple "View page source" would reveal it otherwise).
#
# No booking in the past: the "Book" button only appears
# for today and the following days (and the business layer would refuse it
# anyway).
#
# Security: all the /schedule URLs require an authenticated user
# (see auth/security.py: everything that is not @public). @roles_required
# on an action additionally requires one of the listed roles. Without a valid token:
# back to /login; insufficient role: 403 page.
# =========================================================================
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

from flask import Blueprint, abort, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.security import roles_required
from rdvmedecins.domain.schedule import DoctorDaySchedule
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Person, Role
from rdvmedecins.business import dates
from rdvmedecins.business.exception import BusinessException
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import (ScheduleModel, ScheduleView, ScheduleRowView, Message,
                                            OptionView, BookingView)
from rdvmedecins.web import utils
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_error, flash_success
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

schedule = Blueprint("schedule", __name__, url_prefix="/schedule")


# what the controller knows about the user, to decide what to display
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rights:
    manager: bool  # ADMIN or DOCTOR
    patient: Client | None  # the connected client (USER role), otherwise None
    patient_can_book: bool  # USER without an upcoming appointment


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /schedule
# The URL parameters are read raw (request.args.get), to
# distinguish a MISSING parameter (None) from an EMPTY parameter (?doctorId=).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@schedule.get("")
def show():
    error = None
    user = utils.user()
    rights = compute_rights()

    # the day: that of the URL if it is valid, otherwise today
    day = dates.today()
    raw_day = request.args.get("day")
    if raw_day is not None:
        requested_day = utils.valid_date(raw_day)
        if requested_day is not None:
            day = requested_day
        else:
            error = "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE"
    day_bookable = day >= dates.today()

    # the doctor: that of the URL; failing that, for a connected doctor, themselves
    raw_doctor_id = request.args.get("doctorId")
    doctor_id = utils.positive_integer(raw_doctor_id)
    if raw_doctor_id is None and user.role == Role.DOCTOR:
        doctor = application().get_doctor_by_user_id(user.user_id)
        doctor_id = doctor.id if doctor else None

    # the drop-down list of the doctors
    doctors = [option(d, d.id == doctor_id) for d in application().get_all_doctors()]

    # the schedule, if a doctor is chosen (and the date valid)
    view = None
    if doctor_id is not None and error is None:
        doctor_schedule = application().get_doctor_day_schedule(doctor_id, day)
        if doctor_schedule is None:
            error = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND"
        else:
            view = schedule_view(doctor_schedule, rights, day_bookable)

    # the booking dialog: only if the requested slot is
    # bookable by this user
    booking = None
    slot_id = utils.positive_integer(request.args.get("book"))
    if view is not None and slot_id is not None:
        row = next((r for r in view.rows if r.slot_id == slot_id and r.bookable),
                   None)
        if row is not None:
            booking = BookingView(
                row.slot_id,
                row.time,
                [option(c, False) for c in application().get_all_clients()]
                if rights.manager else [],
                utils.label(rights.patient) if rights.patient else None)

    model = ScheduleModel(
        page_title="SCHEDULE.PAGE_TITLE",
        error=Message(error) if error else None,
        doctors=doctors,
        doctor_id=doctor_id,
        day=utils.iso(day),
        schedule=view,
        booking=booking,
        back_url=schedule_url(doctor_id, day) if doctor_id is not None else url_for("schedule.show"),
        info=patient_info(rights, view))
    return render_template("schedule.html", model=model)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /schedule/book   fields: doctorId, day, slotId, clientId
#
# For a patient (USER), the clientId field is IGNORED: they always book
# for themselves. Trusting a field sent by the
# browser would allow a clever patient to book in the name of another one.
#
# "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern: whatever the result, no page is
# built here - a flash message is set and we redirect
# to the schedule (see example 20).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@schedule.post("/book")
@roles_required(Role.ADMIN, Role.DOCTOR, Role.USER)
def book():
    doctor_id, day = read_schedule_request()
    slot_id = utils.positive_integer(request.form.get("slotId"))
    if doctor_id is None or slot_id is None:
        abort(400)  # -> "invalid request" page (see web/errors.py)
    user = utils.user()

    if user.is_patient:
        client = utils.connected_patient(application())
    else:
        client_id = utils.positive_integer(request.form.get("clientId"))
        if client_id is None:
            # no patient chosen: the booking dialog is opened again
            flash_error("ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT")
            return redirect(schedule_url(doctor_id, day, slot_id))
        client = application().get_client_by_id(client_id)

    slot = application().get_slot_by_id(slot_id)
    if client is None:
        flash_error("ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND")
    elif slot is None or slot.doctor_id != doctor_id:
        flash_error("ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        try:
            # the rules (not in the past, a single upcoming appointment per
            # patient, free slot) are checked by the business layer
            application().add_appointment(day, slot, client)
            flash_success("SCHEDULE.BOOKED")
        except BusinessException as e:
            # same rule, but a message in the 2nd person when it is the
            # patient themselves who books ("You already have..." rather
            # than "This patient..."). The other exceptions (real
            # anomalies) are not caught: 500 page.
            if e.key == "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT" and user.is_patient:
                flash_error("SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO")
            else:
                flash_error(e.key, **e.params)
    return redirect(schedule_url(doctor_id, day))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /schedule/cancel   fields: appointmentId, doctorId, day
# (a patient cancels THEIR appointment from "My area", not from here)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@schedule.post("/cancel")
@roles_required(Role.ADMIN, Role.DOCTOR)
def cancel():
    doctor_id, day = read_schedule_request()
    appointment_id = utils.positive_integer(request.form.get("appointmentId"))
    if doctor_id is None or appointment_id is None:
        abort(400)
    appointment = application().get_appointment_by_id(appointment_id)
    if appointment is None:
        # already cancelled (by someone else, or double click)
        flash_error("ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        application().delete_appointment(appointment)
        flash_success("SCHEDULE.CANCELLED")
    return redirect(schedule_url(doctor_id, day))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# who is connected, and what are they allowed to do on this page?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def compute_rights() -> Rights:
    if not utils.user().is_patient:
        return Rights(True, None, False)
    patient = utils.connected_patient(application())
    upcoming = application().get_client_upcoming_appointments(patient.id)
    return Rights(False, patient, not upcoming)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the doctor's schedule, formatted for the view - and filtered according to the rights
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def schedule_view(doctor_schedule: DoctorDaySchedule, rights: Rights, day_bookable: bool) -> ScheduleView:
    doctor_id = doctor_schedule.doctor.id
    day = doctor_schedule.day
    rows = []
    for dds in doctor_schedule.doctor_day_slots:
        slot, appointment = dds.slot, dds.appointment
        free = appointment is None
        # the appointment of the connected patient?
        mine = appointment is not None and rights.patient is not None and appointment.client_id == rights.patient.id
        rows.append(ScheduleRowView(
            slot_id=slot.id,
            time=utils.time(slot),
            free=free,
            # THE confidentiality point: a patient only receives the name
            # of THEIR appointment; for the others, None (the view displays "Booked")
            patient=utils.label(appointment.client) if appointment is not None and (rights.manager or mine) else None,
            mine=mine,
            bookable=free and day_bookable and (rights.manager or rights.patient_can_book),
            book_url=schedule_url(doctor_id, day, slot.id),
            appointment_id=appointment.id if appointment is not None and rights.manager else None))
    return ScheduleView(utils.label(doctor_schedule.doctor), utils.format_day(day), rows)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- utility functions

# the hidden fields doctorId / day of the POST forms; (None, None) if they are invalid
def read_schedule_request() -> tuple[int | None, date | None]:
    doctor_id = utils.positive_integer(request.form.get("doctorId"))
    day = utils.valid_date(request.form.get("day"))
    return (None, None) if doctor_id is None or day is None else (doctor_id, day)


# /schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-23[&book=7]: url_for adds at the end of
# the URL the parameters that are not variables of the path
def schedule_url(doctor_id: int, day: date, book: int | None = None) -> str:
    if book is None:
        return url_for("schedule.show", doctorId=doctor_id, day=utils.iso(day))
    return url_for("schedule.show", doctorId=doctor_id, day=utils.iso(day), book=book)


def option(p: Person, selected: bool) -> OptionView:
    return OptionView(p.id, utils.label(p), selected)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the information message of a patient who already has an upcoming appointment
# (why there is no "Book" button), or None. Useless if THEIR
# appointment appears in the displayed schedule (in blue): this is the case just
# after they have just booked it, when the message would be out of place.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def patient_info(rights: Rights, view: ScheduleView | None) -> str | None:
    if rights.patient is None or rights.patient_can_book:
        return None
    appointment_shown = view is not None and any(row.mine for row in view.rows)
    return None if appointment_shown else "SCHEDULE.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO"

docs.title: 11.16.2.1. The URL for the page
docs.text: The entire page is described by its URL: [/schedule?doctorId=1&day=2026-09-26] displays Doctor #1’s schedule for that day; [&book=4] also opens the booking window for slot #4. The appointment booking window is therefore not opened by [JavaScript]: the server generates a page containing the window. This means you can reload the page, bookmark it, use the browser’s “Back” button, and the application works without [JavaScript] (the application’s only script is used for confirmation windows, and it works without it as well; see example 21).

docs.title: 11.16.2.2. GET /schedule
docs.text:
• lines 65–68: what the action knows about the user to determine the display: a “manager” (ADMIN or DOCTOR) or a patient, who may or may not make a reservation;
  • lines 83–91: the day: the day specified by URL if it is valid; otherwise, today. Parameters are read in raw format ([request.args.get]) to distinguish between a missing parameter ([None]: the default value is used, with no error) and an invalid parameter (an error is reported). Only today and the following days are bookable;
  • lines 94–98: the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves: a doctor can view their daily schedule directly upon logging in;
  • line 101: the drop-down list of doctors, read from the cache, with the selected doctor highlighted;
  • lines 104–110: the schedule, if a doctor is selected and the date is valid. A nonexistent doctor (an ID manually modified in URL) triggers an error message, not an error page;
  • lines 114–125: the booking window, only if the requested time slot exists and is bookable by this user: a patient who adds [&book=2] to URL for a time slot that is already booked will see nothing. [next(...)] searches for the corresponding calendar entry (example 21). The window displays a list of patients to an administrator; for each patient, it displays their own name;
  • Lines 127–137: The page template. [back_url] is the URL for the calendar without the booking window; the "Cancel" button in the window takes you there.

docs.title: 11.16.2.3. POST /schedule/book
docs.text:
• line 152: All roles can make reservations. The decorator documents the rule and protects it in case a fourth role were to appear in the future;
  • lines 154–157: the form’s hidden fields. Invalid fields can only result from a manually crafted request: error 400;
  • lines 160–168: the patient for the appointment. For a patient, it is always the patient themselves: the field [clientId] is ignored. Trusting a field sent by the browser would allow a patient to book on behalf of another. For an administrator who has not selected a patient, the booking window reopens with a message;
  • lines 170–189: validations (the patient exists, the time slot exists and belongs to the doctor in the calendar), followed by the booking. Business rules are verified by the business logic layer; a [BusinessException] becomes a flash error message. The message “only one upcoming appointment” is adapted when the patient makes the booking themselves (“You already have...” rather than “This patient already has...”);
  • line 190: in all cases, return to the calendar (schema PRG).

docs.title: 11.16.2.4. POST /schedule/cancel
docs.text: • Lines 197–211: Canceling an appointment, reserved for administrators (a patient cancels their appointment from their account). An appointment that has already been canceled (by someone else or by double-clicking) displays a message, not an error.

docs.title: 11.16.2.5. Permissions, the formatted calendar, and utility functions
docs.text:
• lines 217–222: user permissions. For a patient, it is necessary to view their upcoming appointments: an empty list is “incorrect,” hence [not upcoming];
  • lines 228–248: the domain’s calendar, formatted for display and filtered according to permissions. This is where patient confidentiality comes into play (line 243): for a patient, the names of other patients are not merely hidden from view; they are never included in the template. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it, even if hidden (otherwise, a simple “View Source” would reveal it). The “Book” button appears only when there is an available time slot, a bookable day, and a user with the right to make a reservation; the “Cancel” button appears only for an administrator;
  • lines 254–257: the hidden fields [doctorId] and [day] in the POST forms, validated;
  • lines 262–265: the URL from the calendar. [url_for] adds the named parameters that are not path variables to URL as parameters (example 16);
  • lines 278–282: the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment: it explains why the “Book” buttons are missing. It is not displayed if the patient’s own appointment appears in the calendar (in blue), which is the case immediately after booking. [any(...)] returns [True] if either condition is true.

docs.title: 11.16.3. controllers/persons.py
docs.text:
The management of doctors and clients, reserved for the administrator, is identical: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than writing the same actions twice, we write them once, in a blueprint factory.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/persons.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The management of the doctors and that of the clients (reserved for the ADMIN) are
# IDENTICAL: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
# writing the same actions twice, they are written once in a
# BLUEPRINT FACTORY: the create_blueprint function builds a
# complete blueprint, from a "configuration" that says WHAT to call and
# WHICH labels to display. controllers/doctors.py and controllers/clients.py
# each call it with their own. We thus get, for each of them:
#
#   GET  /doctors                    list
#   GET  /doctors/add                empty form
#   POST /doctors/add                creation
#   GET  /doctors/<id>/edit          pre-filled form
#   POST /doctors/<id>/edit          edit
#   POST /doctors/<id>/delete        deletion
#
# (and the same URLs under /clients). The views are common as well:
# templates/persons/list.html and templates/persons/form.html.
#
# SECURITY: a before_request OF THE BLUEPRINT requires the ADMIN role. It
# runs before EACH action of the blueprint - including those that would be
# added to it later: the rule is written once and for all.
# =========================================================================
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from flask import Blueprint, abort, redirect, render_template, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.security import require_roles
from rdvmedecins.entities import Person, Role
from rdvmedecins.forms.forms import PersonForm
from rdvmedecins.business.person_data import PersonData
from rdvmedecins.business.exception import BusinessException
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import (PersonKeys, FormState, PersonFormModel,
                                            PersonListModel, Message, PersonView,
                                            PersonValues)
from rdvmedecins.web import validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_error, flash_success


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# what each type of person must provide. The last five fields
# are FUNCTIONS: doctors.py and clients.py put lambdas in them that
# call the methods of the ApplicationModel (get_all_doctors...).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonsConfig:
    name: str  # "doctors" or "clients": the name of the blueprint, and the start of the URLs
    keys: PersonKeys
    list: Callable[[], list[Person]]  # () -> list
    find: Callable[[int], Person | None]  # id -> person
    add: Callable[[PersonData], Person]  # data -> created person
    edit: Callable[[int, PersonData], Person]  # (id, data) -> edited person
    delete: Callable[[int], None]  # id -> nothing


def create_blueprint(config: PersonsConfig) -> Blueprint:
    bp = Blueprint(config.name, __name__, url_prefix=f"/{config.name}")

    # the URL of an action of THIS blueprint: url("list_persons") -> "/doctors"
    def url(action: str, **params) -> str:
        return url_for(f"{config.name}.{action}", **params)

    # all the actions of the blueprint are reserved for the ADMIN
    @bp.before_request
    def admin_only():
        require_roles(Role.ADMIN)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GET /doctors (or /clients)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("")
    def list_persons():
        persons = [PersonView(p.title, p.first_name, p.last_name, login(p),
                              url("edit_form", id=p.id),
                              url("delete", id=p.id))
                   for p in config.list()]
        model = PersonListModel(config.keys.title, None, config.keys, url("add_form"),
                                persons)
        return render_template("persons/list.html", model=model)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GET /doctors/add
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("/add")
    def add_form():
        return show_form(None, PersonValues(), {}, None, None)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # POST /doctors/add
    # PersonForm() reads the input; validate() checks it.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/add")
    def add():
        form = PersonForm()
        if not form.validate():
            return show_form(None, entered_values(form), validation.errors_of(form),
                             None, None)
        try:
            person = config.add(data(form))
        except BusinessException as e:
            return show_business_error(None, entered_values(form), e)
        flash_success(config.keys.added, **params(person))
        return redirect(url("list_persons"))

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GET /doctors/<id>/edit
    # <int:id>: the id must be made of digits - /doctors/abc/edit does
    # not match any route (404 page)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("/<int:id>/edit")
    def edit_form(id: int):
        person = config.find(id)
        if person is None:
            abort(404)
        values = PersonValues(person.title, person.first_name, person.last_name, login(person),
                              person.version)
        return show_form(id, values, {}, None, None)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # POST /doctors/<id>/edit
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/<int:id>/edit")
    def edit(id: int):
        form = PersonForm()
        if not form.validate():
            return show_form(id, entered_values(form), validation.errors_of(form),
                             None, None)
        try:
            person = config.edit(id, data(form))
        except BusinessException as e:
            return show_business_error(id, entered_values(form), e)
        flash_success(config.keys.edited, **params(person))
        return redirect(url("list_persons"))

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # POST /doctors/<id>/delete
    # (the "Are you sure?" confirmation is requested before the form
    # is sent, see static/js/app.js)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/<int:id>/delete")
    def delete(id: int):
        person = config.find(id)
        try:
            config.delete(id)
            flash_success(config.keys.deleted, **params(person))
        except BusinessException as e:
            flash_error(e.key, **e.params)
        return redirect(url("list_persons"))

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

    # id None: creation form; otherwise: edit form.
    # errors: field -> key of the message; error: the key of the message at the bottom
    # of the page; other_fields: additional fields to outline in red
    def show_form(id: int | None, values: PersonValues, errors: dict[str, str],
                  error: str | None, other_fields: list[str] | None):
        creating = id is None
        state: FormState = validation.state(errors, other_fields)
        model = PersonFormModel(
            page_title=config.keys.add if creating else config.keys.edit,
            error=validation.page_message(errors, Message(error) if error else None),
            values=values,
            state=state,
            creating=creating,
            action=url("add") if creating else url("edit", id=id),
            list_url=url("list_persons"))
        return render_template("persons/form.html", model=model)

    # a business rule has refused the write: the form is displayed again,
    # with the user's input and the message of the business layer
    def show_business_error(id: int | None, values: PersonValues, e: BusinessException):
        if e.key in ("ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND", "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND"):
            # deleted in the meantime by another ADMIN: back to the list
            flash_error(e.key)
            return redirect(url("list_persons"))
        # the message goes at the bottom of the page; the fields concerned, if any, are
        # outlined in red so that the user immediately sees what to correct
        return show_form(id, values, {}, e.key, validation.BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.key))

    return bp


# what the user has typed (password excluded: it is never sent back
# to the browser). form.<field>.data: the value, after the filters
def entered_values(form: PersonForm) -> PersonValues:
    return PersonValues(form.title.data or "", form.first_name.data or "", form.last_name.data or "",
                        form.login.data or "", form.version.data)


# the validated form -> the data expected by the business layer
def data(form: PersonForm) -> PersonData:
    return PersonData(form.title.data, form.last_name.data, form.first_name.data, form.login.data,
                      form.password.data, form.version.data)


# {name} and {login} of the "added / edited / deleted" messages
def params(person: Person | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    if person is None:
        return {"name": "", "login": ""}
    return {"name": f"{person.first_name} {person.last_name}", "login": login(person)}


def login(person: Person) -> str:
    return person.user.login if person.user else ""
  • lines 49–56: what each type of entity must provide: the blueprint name (which is also the beginning of URL), the translation keys, and five functions: list, find, add, edit, and delete. This is the same process as for business layer descriptors;
  • Lines 59–60: The factory creates a blueprint, whose name and the prefix of URL come from the configuration. The actions are internal functions of [create_blueprint]: they have access to the factory’s variable [config]. Each call to [create_blueprint] creates a new blueprint, with its own actions;
  • lines 63–64: the URL for an action in this blueprint: [url("list_persons")] returns [/doctors] for the doctors’ blueprint and [/clients] for the clients’ blueprint;
  • lines 67–69: a blueprint [before_request]: it runs before every action in the blueprint (and only in this one), after those of the application. All actions are thus reserved for the administrator, including any that might be added later: the rule is written once and applies to all;
  • lines 74–82: the list. [@bp.get("")]: the route is the prefix of the blueprint itself ([/doctors]);
  • lines 95–106: the add operation: form validation (input errors, displayed below the fields), call to the business layer (business errors, displayed at the bottom of the page), followed by a flash message and redirection to the list. The flash messages receive parameters: the person’s name and login;
  • lines 113–120: the edit form, pre-filled with the record’s version (optimistic locking). A nonexistent person results in a 404 page;
  • lines 125–136: the update, modeled after the add operation;
  • lines 143–151: the delete operation, confirmed beforehand by the confirmation window (example 21). A rejection by the business layer (a doctor who has appointments) results in a flash error message;
  • lines 158–170: the add form ([id] equals [None]) or edit form, along with its status (values, errors, fields highlighted in red);
  • lines 174–181: a business error: a person who has since been deleted by another administrator is returned to the list; the others redisplay the form, with the relevant fields highlighted in red;
  • lines 188–190: the values to be redisplayed: what the user entered, never the password;
  • lines 194–196: the validated form, converted into data for the business layer;
  • lines 200–203: the parameters for the “added/modified/deleted” messages.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/doctors.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Management of the doctors (ADMIN role only). All the actions are
# built by controllers/persons.py: all that remains here is to say WHAT
# to call and WHICH labels to display.
#
# The functions of the configuration are LAMBDAS (functions without a
# name, written on the spot): application() is only called when
# the action runs, during a request - the ApplicationModel does not exist
# yet when this module is imported.
# =========================================================================
from rdvmedecins.controllers.persons import PersonsConfig, create_blueprint
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import PersonKeys
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

doctors = create_blueprint(PersonsConfig(
    name="doctors",
    keys=PersonKeys(
        title="DOCTORS.TITLE",
        add="DOCTORS.ADD",
        edit="DOCTORS.EDIT",
        empty="DOCTORS.EMPTY",
        confirm_delete="DOCTORS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
        added="DOCTORS.ADDED",
        edited="DOCTORS.UPDATED",
        deleted="DOCTORS.DELETED"),
    list=lambda: application().get_all_doctors(),
    find=lambda id: application().get_doctor_by_id(id),
    add=lambda data: application().add_doctor(data),
    edit=lambda id, data: application().edit_doctor(id, data),
    delete=lambda id: application().delete_doctor(id)))

The doctors’ blueprint, generated by [create_blueprint] along with its configuration. The configuration functions are anonymous functions ([lambda]), which call [ApplicationModel]. Why not write [list=application().get_all_doctors] directly? Because this module is executed when it is imported, at startup, before the application is created: [application()], which requires [current_app], would fail. The anonymous function defers the call until the action is executed, during a request.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/clients.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Management of the clients (the PATIENTS of the practice), ADMIN role only.
# Same principle as controllers/doctors.py (see its comments).
# =========================================================================
from rdvmedecins.controllers.persons import PersonsConfig, create_blueprint
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import PersonKeys
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

clients = create_blueprint(PersonsConfig(
    name="clients",
    keys=PersonKeys(
        title="CLIENTS.TITLE",
        add="CLIENTS.ADD",
        edit="CLIENTS.EDIT",
        empty="CLIENTS.EMPTY",
        confirm_delete="CLIENTS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
        added="CLIENTS.ADDED",
        edited="CLIENTS.UPDATED",
        deleted="CLIENTS.DELETED"),
    list=lambda: application().get_all_clients(),
    find=lambda id: application().get_client_by_id(id),
    add=lambda data: application().add_client(data),
    edit=lambda id, data: application().edit_client(id, data),
    delete=lambda id: application().delete_client(id)))

The client blueprint, following the same pattern.
