docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# controllers/registration.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Create a patient account": a patient who does not have an account yet
# creates it themselves. PUBLIC routes (one does not have an account yet, by
# definition):
#
#   POST /register/access     "Create a patient account" button of the
#                             authentication page: checks the captcha of
#                             THAT page, then opens the form
#   GET  /register            the form
#   POST /register            the creation, then back to the login page
#
# The flow is protected against robots by ONE captcha, that of the
# authentication page:
#   1. the "Create a patient account" button sends the login form
#      to /register/access; if the captcha is typed correctly, the server
#      issues a pass (see auth/registration_pass.py);
#   2. without a valid pass, /register sends back to the
#      authentication page - typing the URL directly is useless;
#   3. the pass is consumed on creation: one solved captcha
#      makes it possible to create ONE account;
#   4. in addition, the number of accounts created per hour and per IP address is
#      limited (see auth/limiter.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one the ADMIN would create from the
# "Patients" page (same method of the business layer: add_client), except
# that the patient CHOOSES their login and their password (mandatory,
# with confirmation).
# =========================================================================
from flask import Blueprint, current_app, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth import registration_pass
from rdvmedecins.auth.security import public
from rdvmedecins.controllers.auth import ip_address
from rdvmedecins.forms.forms import RegistrationForm
from rdvmedecins.business.person_data import PersonData
from rdvmedecins.business.exception import BusinessException
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import RegistrationModel, Message, PersonValues
from rdvmedecins.web import validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_error, flash_success
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application, captchas, limiter, passes

registration = Blueprint("registration", __name__, url_prefix="/register")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /register/access   fields: captchaId, captcha (those of the
# authentication page; login and password, also sent, are ignored)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@registration.post("/access")
@public
def access():
    ip = ip_address()

    # too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to go further
    minutes = limiter().registration_block_minutes(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        flash_error("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", minutes=str(minutes))
        return redirect(url_for("auth.show_login"))

    # captcha missing or wrong: back to the authentication page, with
    # a new image (a failure counts as a login failure)
    if not captchas().verify(request.form.get("captchaId"), request.form.get("captcha")):
        limiter().login_failure(ip, "")
        flash_error("ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT")
        return redirect(url_for("auth.show_login"))

    # correct captcha: the pass is issued and the form is opened
    response = redirect(url_for("registration.form"))
    registration_pass.set_cookie(response, passes().issue(), current_app.config["COOKIE_SECURE"])
    return response


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /register
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@registration.get("")
@public
def form():
    if not passes().is_valid(request.cookies.get(registration_pass.COOKIE)):
        return back_to_login()
    return show(PersonValues(), {}, None, None)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /register
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@registration.post("")
@public
def create():
    pass_id = request.cookies.get(registration_pass.COOKIE)
    if not passes().is_valid(pass_id):
        return back_to_login()
    ip = ip_address()
    form = RegistrationForm()
    form.validate()
    values = PersonValues(form.title.data or "Mr", form.first_name.data or "",
                          form.last_name.data or "", form.login.data or "", None)

    # 1. too many accounts created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiter().registration_block_minutes(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return show(values, {}, Message("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", {"minutes": str(minutes)}),
                    None)

    # 2. all the input errors at once (fields + confirmation):
    #    the user corrects them all in one go
    errors = validation.errors_of(form)
    if "password" not in errors and "confirmation" not in errors \
            and form.password.data != form.confirmation.data:
        errors["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"
    if errors:
        return show(values, errors, None, None)

    # 3. the creation (client + USER account, in a transaction)
    try:
        application().add_client(PersonData(form.title.data, form.last_name.data,
                                            form.first_name.data, form.login.data,
                                            form.password.data))
    except BusinessException as e:
        # login or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return show(values, {}, Message(e.key), validation.BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.key))

    # 4. the pass has been used: it will not allow creating a 2nd account
    passes().consume(pass_id)
    limiter().registration_success(ip)

    # 5. back to the login page, login pre-filled
    flash_success("REGISTRATION.DONE", login=form.login.data)
    response = redirect(url_for("auth.show_login", login=form.login.data))
    registration_pass.clear_cookie(response)
    return response


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

# no valid pass: back to the authentication page
def back_to_login():
    flash_error("ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT")
    return redirect(url_for("auth.show_login"))


# the form; never a password sent back to the browser
def show(values: PersonValues, errors: dict[str, str], error: Message | None,
         other_fields: list[str] | None):
    model = RegistrationModel("REGISTRATION.TITLE", validation.page_message(errors, error),
                              values, validation.state(errors, other_fields))
    return render_template("registration.html", model=model)
  • Lines 51–72: The “Create a patient account” button on the login page submits the login form to this action (using the [formaction] attribute, Example 20). It checks the limit on account creations, then the CAPTCHA on the login page; if it is correct, it issues a token ([auth/registration_pass.py]) and redirects to the registration form. A failure is counted as a failed login attempt (with an empty username);
  • lines 78–83: the form, only with a valid passcode: typing the address [/register] directly redirects to the login page;
  • lines 89–133: account creation: - the passcode, again; - [form.validate()] is called, but its result is ignored: we want all input errors at once, including any mismatch between the password and its confirmation, which is then verified by the action (provided both fields are otherwise valid). The user corrects them all at once; - the client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator; - the pass is consumed, and the creation is counted by the limiter; - return to the login page, with a message and the login pre-filled (parameter [login] from URL). The pass cookie is cleared.

docs.title: 11.16.6. controllers/area.py
docs.text:
The patient’s personal pages.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/area.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The PERSONAL pages of the patient (USER role), the one they see right
# after logging in:
#
#   GET  /my-area                  home page: [Manage my account],
#                                  [View a schedule], and their upcoming appointment
#   POST /my-area/cancel           cancels THEIR appointment
#   GET  /my-account               form to edit their account
#   POST /my-account               edit
#   POST /my-account/delete        deletion of the account (and of its appointments)
#
# Golden rule of this controller: the patient concerned is ALWAYS the one of the
# token (utils.connected_patient), never an identifier sent by the
# browser. A patient can therefore neither see, nor edit, nor cancel what
# belongs to another patient, even by crafting their requests themselves.
#
# Any edit or deletion of the account requires the CURRENT
# password: someone who found a session left open could
# neither change the password, nor delete the account. Wrong current
# password errors are counted as login failures (same limit).
# =========================================================================
from flask import Blueprint, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.auth_service import AuthService
from rdvmedecins.auth.security import require_roles
from rdvmedecins.controllers.auth import ip_address
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Role
from rdvmedecins.forms.forms import MyAccountForm
from rdvmedecins.business.person_data import PersonData
from rdvmedecins.business.exception import BusinessException
from rdvmedecins.models.view_models import (AreaModel, Message, MyAccountModel, AppointmentView,
                                            PersonValues)
from rdvmedecins.web import utils, validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_error, flash_success
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application, auth_service, limiter

area = Blueprint("area", __name__)


# all the actions of this blueprint are reserved for the USER role
@area.before_request
def patient_only():
    require_roles(Role.USER)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-area
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@area.get("/my-area")
def patient_area():
    patient = utils.connected_patient(application())
    appointments = [AppointmentView(
        a.id,
        utils.format_day(a.day),
        utils.time(a.slot),
        utils.label(a.slot.doctor),
        # link to the doctor's schedule on that day: the patient sees their name there
        url_for("schedule.show", doctorId=a.slot.doctor_id, day=utils.iso(a.day)))
        for a in application().get_client_upcoming_appointments(patient.id)]
    model = AreaModel("AREA.TITLE", None, utils.label(patient), appointments)
    return render_template("area.html", model=model)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-area/cancel   field: appointmentId
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@area.post("/my-area/cancel")
def cancel_appointment():
    patient = utils.connected_patient(application())
    appointment_id = utils.positive_integer(request.form.get("appointmentId"))
    appointment = application().get_appointment_by_id(appointment_id) if appointment_id is not None else None
    # an appointment that does not exist, and that of ANOTHER patient, receive
    # the same response: nothing is revealed about the appointments of others
    if appointment is None or appointment.client_id != patient.id:
        flash_error("ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        application().delete_appointment(appointment)
        flash_success("SCHEDULE.CANCELLED")
    return redirect(url_for("area.patient_area"))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@area.get("/my-account")
def account_form():
    patient = utils.connected_patient(application())
    values = PersonValues(patient.title, patient.first_name, patient.last_name, patient.user.login,
                          patient.version)
    return show(values, {}, None, None)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@area.post("/my-account")
def edit_account():
    patient = utils.connected_patient(application())
    form = MyAccountForm()
    form.validate()
    values = PersonValues(form.title.data or patient.title, form.first_name.data or "",
                          form.last_name.data or "", form.login.data or "", form.version.data)

    errors = validation.errors_of(form)
    if "password" not in errors and form.password.data is not None \
            and form.password.data != form.confirmation.data:
        errors["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"
    if errors:
        return show(values, errors, None, None)

    # the current password
    password_error = check_current_password(patient, form.current_password.data)
    if password_error is not None:
        # wrong password: the message also goes UNDER the field
        field_errors = ({"current_password": password_error.key}
                        if password_error.key == "ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD" else {})
        return show(values, field_errors, password_error, None)

    try:
        client = application().edit_client(patient.id, PersonData(
            form.title.data, form.last_name.data, form.first_name.data, form.login.data,
            form.password.data,  # None = unchanged
            form.version.data))
    except BusinessException as e:
        return show(values, {}, Message(e.key), validation.BUSINESS_ERROR_FIELDS.get(e.key))
    # the login and the displayed name are IN the token: a new one is
    # issued, otherwise the navigation bar would keep the old name
    flash_success("MY_ACCOUNT.UPDATED")
    response = redirect(url_for("area.patient_area"))
    auth_service().set_token(response, client.user)
    return response


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account/delete   field: delete_password
# The account, the client and ALL their appointments disappear together,
# then the patient is logged out.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@area.post("/my-account/delete")
def delete_account():
    patient = utils.connected_patient(application())
    password_error = check_current_password(
        patient, request.form.get("delete_password"))
    if password_error is not None:
        flash_error(password_error.key, **password_error.params)
        return redirect(url_for("area.account_form"))
    application().delete_client(patient.id)
    flash_success("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETED")
    response = redirect(url_for("auth.show_login"))
    AuthService.clear_token(response)
    return response


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

# None if the current password is correct; otherwise the error message
def check_current_password(patient: Client, password: str | None) -> Message | None:
    ip = ip_address()
    login = patient.user.login
    minutes = limiter().login_block_minutes(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return Message("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", {"minutes": str(minutes)})
    ok = bool(password) and auth_service().validate_user(login, password) is not None
    if not ok:
        limiter().login_failure(ip, login)
        return Message("ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD")
    return None


def show(values: PersonValues, errors: dict[str, str], error: Message | None,
         other_fields: list[str] | None):
    model = MyAccountModel("MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE", validation.page_message(errors, error), values,
                           validation.state(errors, other_fields))
    return render_template("account.html", model=model)
  • lines 43–45: All actions in the blueprint are reserved for the USER role;
  • lines 51–63: the patient’s dashboard: their upcoming appointments, formatted, each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day. The patient is always the one associated with the token ([utils.connected_patient]), never an identifier sent by the browser: a patient cannot view, modify, or cancel another patient’s information;
  • lines 69–81: Canceling the patient’s appointment. A nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information about other patients’ appointments is disclosed (otherwise, a patient could discover which appointment numbers exist);
  • lines 87–92: the user’s account form, pre-filled;
  • lines 98–133: the edit: validation of fields and confirmation, verification of the current password, then a call to the business layer. The login and the displayed name are in the token: the action issues a new one; otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name until the next login;
  • lines 141–153: account deletion, which is also protected by the current password. The account, the client, and all their appointments are deleted together; the patient is logged out;
  • lines 159–169: The current password protects the account from anyone who might find a session that has been left open. Mistakes are counted as login failures, with the same limit: they cannot be used to guess the password.

docs.title: 11.17. The Views
docs.text: The [templates] folder contains the application’s [Jinja2] views: one template, seven fragments, and eight pages. All follow the same rule: no logic in the views. Actions pass them pre-prepared templates ([models/view_models.py]); the views simply place the data into HTML and translate the text using the [t] function. They contain no hard-coded text: everything goes through the dictionaries.

docs.title: 11.17.1.1. templates/layout.html
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
{# =========================================================================
   templates/layout.html
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   The layout COMMON to all the pages (see example 15): each page
   (schedule.html, login.html...) EXTENDS it ({% extends %}) and fills its block
   [content].

   Jinja2 ESCAPES everything it displays with {{ ... }} (the characters
   < > & " ' become < >...): protection against HTML injection
   via a typed name, for example. To insert HTML as is, it must be
   requested explicitly (safe filter, see fragments/captcha.html).

   Messages: a success is displayed at the TOP of the page, an error at the BOTTOM, on
   a light pink background (errors.html fragment).

   The layout shares the variables of the page: [model] (the view model
   passed by the action, see models/view_models.py), where it reads the key of the
   page title; [language], [user], [path], [t], added to
   all the views by web/common_model.py.
   ========================================================================= #}
<html lang="{{ language }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  {# t(key): the translation of a key; here, the key is a VARIABLE (model.page_title) #}
  <title>{{ t(model.page_title) }} - {{ t("APP.TITLE") }}</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ url_for('static', filename='lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css') }}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/styles.css') }}">
</head>
<body>
  {# the flash messages set by the previous request: read ONCE
     (get_flashed_messages forgets them immediately), then split: the successes
     at the top, the errors at the bottom #}
  {% set flashes = get_flashed_messages(with_categories=true) %}
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include "fragments/navbar.html" %}
    {% include "fragments/flash.html" %}
    <main>
      {% block content %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% include "fragments/errors.html" %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" dialog, hidden until it is needed #}
  {% include "fragments/confirmation.html" %}
  <script src="{{ url_for('static', filename='js/app.js') }}"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • line 22: the page language, provided by the context processor;
  • line 27: the page title. The title key is a variable ([model.page_title]): each page template provides one (the process from Example 22, using the view template instead of a [{% set %}] variable);
  • line 28: [Bootstrap] is part of the application, located in its [static] folder;
  • Line 35: Flash messages are read once by the template; [get_flashed_messages] immediately forgets them, and a second call would return an empty list. With [with_categories=true], the function returns tuples (category, message). The variable [flashes] is then read by the two fragments that display them: success messages at the top, error messages at the bottom. A variable defined by [{% set %}] is visible to the fragments included by [{% include %}];
  • lines 37–42: the navigation bar, success messages, page content, and error area;
  • lines 45–46: the confirmation window and the script that manages it (Example 21).

docs.title: 11.17.1.2. templates/fragments/navbar.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/navbar.html - the navigation bar.

   Title, FR/EN, role, name, logout - and a menu whose entries
   depend on the role: "Doctors" and "Patients" only appear for
   the ADMIN. It is only a display convenience: the real protection is
   the role checks of the actions (a USER who types /doctors by hand
   gets a 403 page). A patient (USER) additionally has their "My area" menu.

   The menu of the current page is highlighted ("active" class):
   [path] is the requested URL (see web/common_model.py). A macro writes
   once the HTML of a menu entry; its optional parameter [prefix]
   (href by default), is the start of the paths for which the entry is active.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% macro entry(href, key, prefix=none) %}
<li class="nav-item">
  <a class="nav-link{{ ' active' if path.startswith(prefix or href) }}" href="{{ href }}">{{ t(key) }}</a>
</li>
{% endmacro %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">{{ t("APP.TITLE") }}</span>

  {% if user %}
  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {% if user.is_patient %}
    {# active for /my-area AND /my-account #}
    {{ entry("/my-area", "APP.MENU_MY_AREA", "/my-") }}
    {% endif %}
    {{ entry("/schedule", "APP.MENU_SCHEDULE") }}
    {% if user.is_admin %}
    {{ entry("/doctors", "APP.MENU_DOCTORS") }}
    {{ entry("/clients", "APP.MENU_PATIENTS") }}
    {% endif %}
  </ul>
  {% else %}
  <div class="me-auto"></div>
  {% endif %}

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), the active language highlighted #}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code in ["fr", "en"] %}
      <a class="btn {{ 'btn-light' if language == code else 'btn-outline-light' }}" href="/language/{{ code }}">{{ code | upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if user %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ user.role }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ user.name }}</span>
    {# the logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and to the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="/logout" class="m-0">
      <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{{ t("APP.LOGOUT") }}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>
  • lines 15–19: a menu item, highlighted (class [active]) if the path of the current page begins with its prefix. The parameter [prefix] is optional ([none] to [Jinja2], just as [None] to [Python]); otherwise, it is the entry’s address ([prefix or href]). The “My area” entry is prefixed with [/my-]: it is active for both [/my-area] and [/my-account];
  • lines 23–37: the menu depends on the role: “My area” for a patient, “Doctors” and “Patients” for the administrator. This is merely a display convenience; the real security comes from role-based controls on actions. A patient who manually enters [/doctors] will receive a 403 error page;
  • lines 42–44: the FR and EN buttons are simply links to [/language/fr] and [/language/en];
  • lines 48–54: role, username, and logout: a POST form reduced to its button, with the anti-CSRF token.

docs.title: 11.17.1.3. templates/fragments/flash.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/flash.html - the SUCCESS messages set by
   the previous action (appointment saved, doctor added...),
   displayed only once, at the top of the page (see web/flash.py).
   An ERROR flash message is displayed at the bottom of the page, by
   fragments/errors.html.

   [flashes]: the list of the (category, message) pairs, read by the layout.
   t(message.key, message.params): the message whose key is
   message.key, with as parameter the dictionary of the values of {name},
   {login}... (see web/translator.py).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% for category, message in flashes if category == "success" %}
<div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ t(message.key, message.params) }}</div>
{% endfor %}
  • line 13: a [for] loop from [Jinja2] can filter its elements: [for ... in ... if condition] iterates only over elements that satisfy the condition. Each element is a pair, with both parts stored in two variables;
  • line 14: the message is a dictionary (see [web/flash.py]): its key and its parameters. The dot notation in [Jinja2] also reads the keys of a dictionary (example 13).

docs.title: 11.17.1.4. templates/fragments/errors.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/errors.html - the error zone, at the BOTTOM of each
   page, on a light pink background (.error-zone class, see static/css/styles.css).

   It groups the two possible sources of error:
     - model.error: the error of the displayed page (refused form, login
       or first + last names already used, invalid date, wrong password...);
     - the error flash messages, set by the previous action before a
       redirect (slot already booked, deletion refused...).

   A for loop can filter its elements: "for ... in ... if condition".
   role="alert": a screen reader announces the message as soon as the page is
   displayed, even if it is at the bottom.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set flash_errors = flashes | selectattr(0, "equalto", "danger") | list %}
{% if model.error or flash_errors %}
<div class="error-zone" role="alert">
  {% if model.error %}
  <div>{{ t(model.error.key, model.error.params) }}</div>
  {% endif %}
  {% for category, message in flash_errors %}
  <div>{{ t(message.key, message.params) }}</div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
{% endif %}
  • line 15: error flash messages, extracted by two filters: [selectattr(0, "equalto", "danger")] keeps only those elements whose [0] attribute (the first element of the pair, the category) is equal to ["danger"]; [list] converts the result into a list (filters of this type return an iterator that can only be traversed once and cannot be checked to see if it is empty);
  • Lines 16–25: The error area combines the two sources of errors: errors from the displayed page (a rejected form, an invalid date) and errors generated by the previous action before a redirect (a time slot already taken, a deletion rejected). The area exists only if there is at least one error.

docs.title: 11.17.1.5. templates/fragments/confirmation.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/confirmation.html - the "Are you sure?" modal dialog.

   It replaces the window.confirm() box of the browser, which can neither be
   styled, nor translated (its buttons stay in the language of the
   browser, not in that of the page).

   A SINGLE dialog for the whole page, hidden (d-none) at first. Its
   labels are translated here, by the server, like the rest of the page;
   the small script static/js/app.js merely displays it, puts in it
   the message specific to the form (data-confirmation attribute), and sends
   the form if the user confirms.

   Same Bootstrap classes as the booking dialog (fragments/booking.html).
   ========================================================================= #}
<div id="confirmation-modal" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="confirmation-modal-title" aria-describedby="confirmation-modal-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="confirmation-modal-title">{{ t("CONFIRMATION.TITLE") }}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="no" aria-label="{{ t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA') }}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="confirmation-modal-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes
             "Cancel this appointment?", and a "Cancel" button would be ambiguous there #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="no">{{ t("CONFIRMATION.NO") }}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="yes">{{ t("CONFIRMATION.YES") }}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The confirmation window from Example 21, with labels translated by the server (the browser’s [window.confirm()] box displays its buttons in the browser’s language, not the page’s language), a close button, and accessibility attributes: [aria-labelledby] and [aria-describedby] refer to the window’s title and message, which screen readers announce when the window opens. The “No, go back” button is preferred over “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context.

docs.title: 11.17.1.6. templates/fragments/captcha.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/captcha.html - the captcha of the authentication page
   (see auth/captcha.py). It protects both the login and the access to
   account creation ("Create a patient account" button).
   A macro, whose parameter is a Captcha object (id, svg).

   The safe filter: the SVG image is inserted AS IS into the page, without
   escaping. It is harmless here because this SVG is built by the
   server itself and contains nothing that comes from the user - one would
   NEVER do that with an input.

   The hidden field captchaId tells the server WHICH captcha to check; the right
   answer itself is never sent to the browser.
   "Another image" simply reloads the page ([path] = the current URL).
   A macro does not see the variables of the page that calls it ("with
   context": it does, on import, see login.html): here, t and path.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% macro captcha(captcha) %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{{ t("CAPTCHA.LABEL") }}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{{ t('CAPTCHA.IMAGE_ALT') }}">{{ captcha.svg | safe }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{{ path }}">{{ t("CAPTCHA.NEW_IMAGE") }}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captchaId" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{{ t("CAPTCHA.HELP") }}</div>
</div>
{% endmacro %}
  • line 18: a macro that receives an object [Captcha];
  • line 22: the SVG image, inserted as-is (example 27). The attribute [role="img"] and its [aria-label] describe the image to screen readers;
  • line 23: the “Another image” link simply reloads the page: each view generates a new CAPTCHA;
  • Lines 25–27: the CAPTCHA ID and the input field. [autocapitalize="off"] and [spellcheck="false"] prevent phones from modifying the input (initial uppercase letter, spell check).

By default, an imported macro cannot access the variables of the page that imports it: the function [t] and the variable [path], provided by the context processor, would be unknown to it. This is why [login.html] imports it with the reference [with context].

docs.title: 11.17.1.7. templates/fragments/person_fields.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/person_fields.html - the identity fields (title,
   first name, last name), common to three forms: doctor/client of the ADMIN,
   "Create a patient account" and "Manage my account".
   The fragment, inserted by {% include %}, reads the [model] variable of the
   page that inserts it (a FormView, see models/view_models.py):
   values, message under each field, fields outlined in red.

   selected: a boolean attribute, written if the option is chosen, omitted otherwise.
   state.invalid_class(field): "is-invalid" (red outline of Bootstrap)
   for a refused field, "" otherwise.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set state = model.state %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="title">{{ t("PERSONS.TITLE_LABEL") }}</label>
  <select id="title" name="title" class="form-select {{ state.invalid_class('title') }}">
    {% for title in model.titles %}
    <option value="{{ title.value }}"{{ " selected" if title.selected }}>{{ title.value }}</option>
    {% endfor %}
  </select>
  {% if state.error_of("title") %}
  <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("title")) }}</div>
  {% endif %}
</div>

<div class="row g-3 mb-3">
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="first_name">{{ t("PERSONS.FIRSTNAME_LABEL") }}</label>
    <input id="first_name" name="first_name" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('first_name') }}" value="{{ model.values.first_name }}">
    {% if state.error_of("first_name") %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("first_name")) }}</div>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="last_name">{{ t("PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL") }}</label>
    <input id="last_name" name="last_name" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('last_name') }}" value="{{ model.values.last_name }}">
    {% if state.error_of("last_name") %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("last_name")) }}</div>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</div>

The identity fields (title, first name, last name), which are common to all three forms in the application. The fragment, inserted by [{% include %}], reads the variable [model] from the page that inserts it: a template that inherits from [FormView].

  • Lines 16–20: the list of titles, calculated by the template’s [titles] property, with the selected title highlighted;
  • lines 29–30: the first name input field, with the value to be redisplayed, and the class [is-invalid] if the field is rejected ([state.invalid_class('first_name')]);
  • lines 31–33: the message below the field, translated.

The attributes [maxlength] and [required] are browser controls. The application’s forms include the attribute [novalidate] (Example 19): these checks are not performed before submission; validation is handled by the server. [maxlength], on the other hand, always prevents users from entering more characters than a column can accommodate.

docs.title: 11.17.1.8. templates/fragments/booking.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/booking.html - the booking dialog of the
   schedule.

   The REAL Bootstrap classes of a modal dialog (.modal,
   .modal-backdrop...), made visible "hard-coded" (show d-block) rather than
   by the JavaScript of Bootstrap. It is the SERVER that decides to display it
   (&book=... parameter of the URL), and closing it amounts to following a link
   to the same page without this parameter.

   The fragment directly reads the [model] variable of the page that inserts it
   (a ScheduleModel).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set booking = model.booking %}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="booking-title">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="/schedule/book" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="booking-title">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE") }}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ model.back_url }}" aria-label="{{ t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA') }}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT", time=booking.time) }}</p>

        {# what the server must know in addition to the chosen patient #}
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ model.doctor_id }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ model.day }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="slotId" value="{{ booking.slot_id }}">

        {# a patient books for themselves: no list to choose from
           (and the server ignores a possible clientId anyway) #}
        {% if booking.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL") }}</span>:
          <strong>{{ booking.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="clientId">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL") }}</label>
        <select id="clientId" name="clientId" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT") }}</option>
          {% for client in booking.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ model.back_url }}">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL") }}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM") }}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

The reservation window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]) rather than via the [JavaScript] of [Bootstrap]: the server decides whether to display it (the [book] parameter of URL), and closing it is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([model.back_url]).

  • Lines 29–31: Hidden fields: information the server needs to know, in addition to the selected patient;
  • lines 35–48: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name is displayed, with no list to choose from (and the server would ignore a [clientId] field anyway). For an administrator, the list of patients—whose first option, with an empty value, prompts a selection—is displayed.

docs.title: 11.17.2.1. templates/login.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/login.html - the login form (see controllers/auth.py).
   An ordinary HTML <form>: the browser itself sends login,
   password and captcha answer in POST /login, without JavaScript. On
   failure, the server sends back THIS page, with the login already typed, a
   NEW captcha and the error, displayed at the bottom of the page by the layout.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{# with context: the macro sees the variables of this page (t, path) #}
{% from "fragments/captcha.html" import captcha with context %}

{% block content %}
{% set login_typed = model.login != "" %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ t("LOGIN.TITLE") }}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="/login">
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          {# autofocus: a boolean attribute, written if the condition is true, omitted otherwise #}
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{ model.login }}" required{{ " autofocus" if not login_typed }}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required{{ " autofocus" if login_typed }}>
        </div>

        {{ captcha(model.captcha) }}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{ t("LOGIN.SUBMIT") }}</button>

        {# no account yet: a patient can create one themselves.
           It is NOT a simple link: it is a second submit button of
           THIS form, which goes to another address (formaction). The
           server checks the captcha above there before opening the
           account creation page (see controllers/registration.py).
           formnovalidate: the browser does not require login and password
           (useless to create an account); it is the server that checks
           the captcha. Enter in a field always triggers the FIRST
           button of the form, "Log in". #}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="/register/access" formnovalidate>{{ t("LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT") }}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{{ t("LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT_HELP") }}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS") }}</span>
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_ADMIN") }}</span></li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_DOCTOR") }}</span></li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_USER") }}</span></li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}
  • line 10: the macro is imported, along with the page context;
  • line 13: the cursor is placed in the login field if it is empty, or in the password field otherwise (after a failed login attempt or after creating an account): the Boolean attribute [autofocus] is set to one or the other;
  • lines 24–30: the values of the [autocomplete] attribute help browser password managers fill out the form;
  • lines 46–47: The “Create a patient account” button is not a link, but a second button to submit this form, which sends it to a different address ([formaction], example 20). The server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page. [formnovalidate]: The browser does not require the username and password, marked as [required], which are unnecessary for creating an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first button on the form, “Log in.”

docs.title: 11.17.2.2. templates/schedule.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/schedule.html - the main page (see controllers/schedule.py).
   Three blocks:
     1. the choice of the doctor and of the day;
     2. the schedule;
     3. the booking dialog (fragments/booking.html).
   A possible error (invalid date, unknown doctor) is displayed at the
   bottom of the page by the layout (see fragments/errors.html).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {# 1. choice of the doctor and of the day: a GET form, which simply
        reloads this page with ?doctorId=...&day=... in the URL #}
  <form method="get" action="/schedule" class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
      <div class="col-sm-5">
        <label class="form-label" for="doctorId">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL") }}</label>
        <select id="doctorId" name="doctorId" class="form-select" required>
          <option value="">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR") }}</option>
          {% for doctor in model.doctors %}
          <option value="{{ doctor.id }}"{{ " selected" if doctor.selected }}>{{ doctor.label }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-4">
        <label class="form-label" for="day">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL") }}</label>
        <input id="day" name="day" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{ model.day }}" required>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-3">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_SCHEDULE") }}</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>

  {# patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no "Book" button #}
  {% if model.info %}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    <span>{{ t(model.info) }}</span>
    <a href="/my-area" class="alert-link">{{ t("APP.MENU_MY_AREA") }}</a>
  </div>
  {% endif %}

  {# 2. the schedule #}
  {% set schedule = model.schedule %}
  {% if schedule %}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{ t("SCHEDULE.TITLE_PREFIX") }} {{ schedule.day }} - {{ schedule.doctor }}</h5>

    {% if schedule.rows %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{{ t("SCHEDULE.COLUMN_SLOT") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("SCHEDULE.COLUMN_STATUS") }}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for row in schedule.rows %}
        <tr class="{{ 'free-slot' if row.bookable }}">
          <td>{{ row.time }}</td>
          <td>
            {# [patient] is filled only if the user is allowed to
               see this name (ADMIN, DOCTOR, or the patient for THEIR
               appointment) - otherwise, simply "Booked" #}
            {% if row.free %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">{{ t("SCHEDULE.FREE") }}</span>
            {% elif row.patient %}
            <span class="badge {{ 'text-bg-primary' if row.mine else 'text-bg-secondary' }}">{{ row.patient }}</span>
            {% else %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{ t("SCHEDULE.BOOKED_BY_OTHER") }}</span>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
          <td>
            {# the displayed buttons have been decided by the controller
               (bookable, appointment_id) according to the role of the user.
               "Book" is a simple link: it reopens this page
               with the booking dialog of this slot #}
            {% if row.bookable %}
            <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{ row.book_url }}">{{ t("SCHEDULE.BOOK") }}</a>
            {% endif %}
            {# "Cancel" MODIFIES data: it is therefore a POST #}
            {% if row.appointment_id %}
            <form method="post" action="/schedule/cancel" class="m-0"
                  data-confirmation="{{ t('SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM') }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{ row.appointment_id }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="doctorId" value="{{ model.doctor_id }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="day" value="{{ model.day }}">
              <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{{ t("SCHEDULE.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT") }}</button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ t("SCHEDULE.NO_SLOTS") }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  {% else %}
  <p class="text-muted">{{ t("SCHEDULE.EMPTY_STATE") }}</p>
  {% endif %}

  {# 3. the booking dialog, only if the URL contains &book=... #}
  {% if model.booking %}
  {% include "fragments/booking.html" %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}
  • Lines 15–34: Selecting a doctor and a day: a GET form (Example 17), which simply reloads the page with the parameters [doctorId] and [day] in URL. The [<input type="date">] field displays its values in the [yyyy-mm-dd] format, regardless of the language in which the browser displays it;
  • lines 37–42: the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment;
  • Lines 61–95: An entry in the schedule. There are three possible statuses: available, booked with the patient’s name (in blue if it’s the logged-in patient’s appointment), or booked without the name (“Booked”). The buttons displayed are determined by the action. “Book” is a simple link: it reopens this page with the reservation window for that time slot. “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form, with its confirmation request (example 21);
  • lines 108–110: the booking window, only if the action has prepared it.

docs.title: 11.17.2.3. templates/persons/list.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/persons/list.html - the list of the doctors OR of the clients (ADMIN).
   A single view for both: the labels specific to each one arrive in
   model.keys (see controllers/doctors.py / controllers/clients.py).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block content %}
  <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
    <h4 class="mb-0">{{ t(model.keys.title) }}</h4>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="{{ model.add_url }}">{{ t(model.keys.add) }}</a>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    {% if model.persons %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONS.COLUMN_TITLE") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONS.COLUMN_FIRSTNAME") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONS.COLUMN_LASTNAME") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONS.COLUMN_LOGIN") }}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for person in model.persons %}
        <tr>
          <td>{{ person.title }}</td>
          <td>{{ person.first_name }}</td>
          <td>{{ person.last_name }}</td>
          <td><code>{{ person.login }}</code></td>
          <td class="text-end">
            <div class="d-inline-flex gap-2">
              <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" href="{{ person.edit_url }}">{{ t("PERSONS.EDIT") }}</a>
              {# data-confirmation: a confirmation dialog will open
                 before the form is sent (see static/js/app.js) #}
              <form method="post" action="{{ person.delete_url }}" class="m-0"
                    data-confirmation="{{ t(model.keys.confirm_delete) }}">
                <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
                <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{{ t("PERSONS.DELETE") }}</button>
              </form>
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ t(model.keys.empty) }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

A single view for both lists, doctors and clients: the labels specific to each appear in [model.keys]; [t(model.keys.title)] renders a key that is itself a variable. Each row has an “Edit” link and a “Delete” form, which requires confirmation.

docs.title: 11.17.2.4. templates/persons/form.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/persons/form.html - creation OR edit of a
   doctor or of a client (ADMIN). model.creating distinguishes the two cases.

   When the input is refused (empty field, login already taken...), the action
   sends back THIS view with:
     - the values already typed (model.values);
     - the faulty fields outlined in red (Bootstrap class "is-invalid");
     - under a field refused by the validation, its message;
     - the error message of the page, displayed AT THE BOTTOM of the page by the
       layout (see fragments/errors.html).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block content %}
{% set state = model.state %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ t(model.page_title) }}</h5>

      {# novalidate: we let the SERVER validate (it is the authority);
         the checks of the browser (required...) are only a convenience,
         that a user can always bypass #}
      <form method="post" action="{{ model.action }}" novalidate>
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        {% if not model.creating %}
        <input type="hidden" name="version" value="{{ model.values.version }}">
        {% endif %}

        {# title, first name, last name: fragment common to three forms #}
        {% include "fragments/person_fields.html" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ t("PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION") }}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="off"
                 class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('login') }}" value="{{ model.values.login }}">
          {% if state.error_of("login") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("login")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_CREATE" if model.creating else "PERSONS.LOGIN_HELP_EDIT") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          {# never pre-filled: the password never goes back to the browser #}
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                 class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('password') }}">
          {% if state.error_of("password") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("password")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_CREATE" if model.creating else "PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("PERSONS.SAVE") }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ model.list_url }}">{{ t("PERSONS.BACK") }}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}
  • line 25: the mailing address is provided by the action: [/doctors/add], [/clients/3/edit]...;
  • lines 27–29: on update, the record version is stored in a hidden field (optimistic lock);
  • line 32: the identity fields;
  • lines 38–44: the login, optional, with a tooltip that depends on whether the record is being created or edited ([t("..." if model.creating else "...")]);
  • lines 50-50: the password is never pre-filled; it is never sent back to the browser. [autocomplete="new-password"] prevents the browser from suggesting the administrator’s password here.

docs.title: 11.17.2.5. templates/registration.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/registration.html - "Create a patient account" (public page,
   see controllers/registration.py). Same identity fields as the form
   of the ADMIN (person_fields.html fragment), but the login and the
   password are mandatory, with confirmation.
   No captcha HERE: one only gets to this page after having typed
   that of the authentication page ("Create a patient account" button).

   t(key, min=...): the message whose key is the value of [key], with the
   {min} parameter (see web/translator.py).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block content %}
{% set state = model.state %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-1">{{ t("REGISTRATION.TITLE") }}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small mb-3">{{ t("REGISTRATION.INTRO") }}</p>

      <form method="post" action="/register" novalidate>
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        {% include "fragments/person_fields.html" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ t("PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION") }}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('login') }}" value="{{ model.values.login }}">
          {% if state.error_of("login") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("login")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("REGISTRATION.LOGIN_HELP") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("PERSONS.PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('password') }}">
            {% if state.error_of("password") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("password"), min=model.password_min) }}</div>
            {% else %}
            <div class="form-text">{{ t("REGISTRATION.PASSWORD_HELP", min=model.password_min) }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">{{ t("ACCOUNT.CONFIRMATION_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('confirmation') }}">
            {% if state.error_of("confirmation") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("confirmation")) }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("REGISTRATION.SUBMIT") }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/login">{{ t("REGISTRATION.BACK_TO_LOGIN") }}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

The patient account creation form: the personal information fields, followed by the username, password, and password confirmation, are required. The message indicating that a password is too short has a parameter specifying the minimum length: [t(state.error_of("password"), min=model.password_min)]. There is no CAPTCHA here: you can only access this page after entering the CAPTCHA from the login page.

docs.title: 11.17.2.6. templates/area.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/area.html - "My area": the home page of the patient
   (USER role), displayed right after they log in.
     - two options: [Manage my account] and [View a schedule];
     - their upcoming appointment, if they have one, with the means to cancel it.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block content %}
  <h4 class="mb-3">{{ t("AREA.HELLO", name=model.patient) }}</h4>

  <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="/my-account">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{{ t("AREA.MANAGE_ACCOUNT") }}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{{ t("AREA.MANAGE_ACCOUNT_HELP") }}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none option-card" href="/schedule">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{{ t("AREA.VIEW_SCHEDULE") }}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{{ t("AREA.VIEW_SCHEDULE_HELP") }}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{ t("AREA.MY_APPOINTMENT") }}</h5>
    {# normally only one (rule "one upcoming appointment at a time"),
       but the page can display several of them. loop.last: last element?
       The else block of a for loop: the list is empty #}
    {% for appointment in model.appointments %}
    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-2 py-2{{ '' if loop.last else ' border-bottom' }}">
      <div>
        <div class="fw-semibold">{{ appointment.day }}, {{ appointment.time }}</div>
        <div class="text-muted">
          <span>{{ appointment.doctor }}</span> -
          <a href="{{ appointment.schedule_url }}">{{ t("AREA.SEE_IN_SCHEDULE") }}</a>
        </div>
      </div>
      <form method="post" action="/my-area/cancel" class="m-0"
            data-confirmation="{{ t('SCHEDULE.CANCEL_CONFIRM') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="appointmentId" value="{{ appointment.id }}">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger">{{ t("AREA.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT") }}</button>
      </form>
    </div>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ t("AREA.NO_APPOINTMENT") }}</p>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

The patient’s dashboard: two large tabs (“Manage my account,” “View a schedule”) and their upcoming appointments. The [for ... else] loop (example 14) displays a message if the list is empty; [loop.last] removes the border below the last appointment. The page can display multiple appointments, even if the management rule allows only one.

docs.title: 11.17.2.7. templates/account.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/account.html - "Manage my account" (USER role).
   Two independent forms on the same page:
     1. the edit (identity, login, optional new password);
     2. the deletion of the account - which also cancels its appointments.
   Both require the CURRENT password.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block content %}
{% set state = model.state %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. edit #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.TITLE") }}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="/my-account" novalidate>
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="version" value="{{ model.values.version }}">

        {% include "fragments/person_fields.html" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ t("PERSONS.ACCOUNT_SECTION") }}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("PERSONS.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('login') }}" value="{{ model.values.login }}">
          {% if state.error_of("login") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("login")) }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.NEW_PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                   class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('password') }}">
            {% if state.error_of("password") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("password"), min=model.password_min) }}</div>
            {% else %}
            <div class="form-text">{{ t("PERSONS.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT") }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">{{ t("ACCOUNT.CONFIRMATION_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                   class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('confirmation') }}">
            {% if state.error_of("confirmation") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("confirmation")) }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="current_password">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="current_password" name="current_password" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required
                 class="form-control {{ state.invalid_class('current_password') }}">
          {% if state.error_of("current_password") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(state.error_of("current_password")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_HELP") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("PERSONS.SAVE") }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/my-area">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.BACK") }}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    {# 2. deletion #}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_TITLE") }}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_HELP") }}</p>
      <form method="post" action="/my-account/delete" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="{{ t('MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_CONFIRM') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="delete_password">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="delete_password" name="delete_password" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">{{ t("MY_ACCOUNT.DELETE_SUBMIT") }}</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

Two independent forms on the same page: account modification (lines 19–73) and account deletion (lines 80–89), confirmed by the confirmation window. Both require the current password, entered in two separate fields (a form submits only its own fields).
